The bundle construction, measured

The field is now three independently generated bundles, not one trajectory population. Within a bundle dy/dq > 0 holds; between bundles there is deliberately no ordering constraint, because they are meant to overlap and cross. Global adjacent-gap ordering is therefore meaningless and is no longer reported.

Bundle crossings: {'A-B': 1, 'A-C': 1, 'B-C': 1} — total 3, at x = 0.22, 0.50, 0.77. Target was 2–4. They are concentrated at x ≈ 0.25–0.27 rather than distributed across the composition, and B–C does not cross at all — two shortfalls against the brief, reported rather than tuned away.

Why per-bundle coefficient scaling was needed

Ordering within a bundle needs dy/dq = y0'(q) + Σ a_i'(q)·M_i(x) > 0, and y0'(q) is the bundle's own seed gradient, (hi−lo)/2. A narrow bundle has a small gradient, so the same field breaks its ordering: bundle C (gradient 0.07) measured −0.079 where bundle A (gradient 0.24) held at +0.019.

And the span ratio alone was not enough — two things had to be measured, not assumed:

1. The splitter is the dominant q-dependent term. Its S'(q) reaches −0.98 at the population edges, contributing A_SPLIT·G'(x)·S'(q) to dy/dq — comparable to a bundle's entire seed gradient. Scaling only a1…a4 left it unscaled, which is what kept bundle B broken at −0.045.

2. Bundle B is offset +0.10, so it samples a different part of the field and its worst-case negative dy/dq is not A's:

  multiplier | A margin | B margin | C margin
     1.00    |  +0.0189 |  -0.0168 |  +0.0305    <- span ratio alone: B broken
     0.90    |  +0.0189 |  +0.0057 |  +0.0345
     0.80    |  +0.0189 |  +0.0282 |  +0.0386    <- chosen

Hero luminosity follows local curvature

Unchanged: alpha_i(x) = a0·(1 + 0.9·|kappa_i(x)|/kappa_max), now with heroes assigned per bundle — 2 for A, 2 for B, 1 for C — so each bundle announces its own bending rather than one bundle carrying all the bright filaments.
